Torlone “Database systems” - McGraw-Hill (1999) DOWNLOADABLE: http://dbbook.dia.uniroma3.it/ Compared to the last Italian version some chapters are missing More bibliobraphy on specific topics (e.g., JPA) listed in the official program page of the course

# Page 6^page=6
Teaching material • Material is available on the WeBeep portal https://webeep.polimi.it/ under “Data bases 2” • Materials include slides of the lectures, exercise sessions, forum, etc.

# Page 7^page=7
Prerequisites • Basics of Database systems • Relational model • SQL (SQL-92) • Relational algebra  See [DB1 + DB2] textbooks • Object oriented design with UML and programming with Java (basic)

# Page 8^page=8
Triggers (SQL) UPDATE tab1 SET..; INSERT INTO tab1 ...; DELETE tab1 ...; Table tab1 UPDATE trigger BEGIN ... END; INSERT trigger BEGIN ... END; DELETE trigger BEGIN ... END; Application

# Page 9^page=9
Ranking data • We are able to store lots of data, but how do we get the best data out of a dataset? • How does SQL accommodate ranking?

# Page 10^page=10
Database architecture and ORM Opening the database box • Physical data management and query optimization • Transaction management • Concurrency control • CC theory, locking techniques • Reliability control • Log and recovery Opening the application box • Mapping objects to tables and methods to transactions • Managing the alignment between object state in main memory and data state in secondary memory • Building advanced queries DB + Log Secondary Store Manager Buffer Manager Access Method Manager Transaction Manager Reliability Manager Query Manager Lock Tables Concurrency Control System Application DBMS JPA Layer

# Page 11^page=11
Related topics addressed in other courses • 056901 - SYSTEMS AND METHODS FOR BIG AND UNSTRUCTURED DATA • Principles and approaches for data storage and management • Unstructured data management (NoSQL) • graph, semantic, column, document, key-value, IR- based databases • Design methodologies for the specification of NoSQL data models • 056895 - STREAMING DATA ANALYTICS • From data streams and time-series to complex event recognition and processing • Streaming Data analytics techniques

# Page 12^page=12
Exam • The exam consists of a written closed-book verification covering all the topics of the course (everything published on WeBeep, including materials for flipped classrooms) • 3 exercises on the 5 main topics, possibly with related theoretical questions 1. Triggers 2. Ranking and skylines 3. Physical DBs/Query optimization 4. DB architecture/technologies (concurrency control etc.) 5. ORM and JPA • No oral exams • Exception: if requested by the teacher

# Page 13^page=13
Exam rules • During the exam: • No books, notes, or electronic devices are allowed • A calculator is allowed • Cheating policies: Communication with other students is strictly prohibited. In this case, students will be asked to exit the classroom (both!). • In the event of plagiarism, students are notified to the appropriate offices and are postponed to a next exam session • Positive marks: If a mark is rejected and the written exam is retaken (simply sitting down and seeing the exam text is sufficient), the previous mark is lost!

# Page 14^page=14
Exam rules Please, check the general rules for the exams at Politecnico: https://www.polimi.it/en/students/didactic-activities-and- degree-examination/exams

# Page 15^page=15
Exam – mobility students • Official rule: Remote examinations are permitted, at the instructor’s discretion and subject to the feasibility of conducting the assessment, only for students officially participating in international mobility programs (documented by a university (Polimi) agreement, such as Erasmus) when the mobility period overlaps with the exam session. • Mobility students may take the DB2 exam at the foreign university during their mobility period, at the same time as the exam in Milan, with the invigilation of an official staff member (professor or other permanent staff at the university) • Prerequisite: finding such a local officer and putting me in contact with him/her at least one week before the exam • No exceptions will be allowed
